images.title: Perpendiculars stay parallel
images.purpose: Show that two perpendiculars to the same base stay the same distance apart, so the top side equals the base.
images.composition: One rectangle centred, with two equal grey double-arrows across it at two heights; wide white margins.
images.exact_structure: One rectangle ABCD, outline teal #0072B2, A bottom left, B bottom right, C top right, D top left, right-angle marks at all 4 corners. Base AB is 8 units wide and sides AD and BC are 5 units tall, drawn exactly vertical. Two thin grey #6B7280 horizontal double-arrows spanning the full width, one at the base and one at the top, same length, each marked with the same tick. Exactly 1 rectangle, 2 arrows, 4 right-angle marks.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
sides that lean inwards or outwards, or arrows of unequal length
images.takeaway: Perpendiculars to one base stay equally far apart, so DC equals AB.
images.description: Rectangle ABCD with two vertical sides and two equal grey arrows at the bottom and the top labelled same distance.
images.context: Shown with the concept as its one key picture, next to the walkthrough video. PLACEHOLDER: specified, not generated yet.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student to compare the two grey arrows and say why the top cannot be shorter.

image_decisions.why: One clean geometry picture carries the single idea of this video.
